description:
Bring every comment and Rustdoc block in the workspace's Rust sources to the documentation contract: current state only, non-obvious content only, shortest form. Source documentation then starts from a clean baseline.

## Background

The root `AGENTS.md` states that comments and Rustdoc carry only what the code leaves non-obvious (the contract, an invariant, the reason behind a choice, or a pointer to evidence), that history belongs in git and the tracker, and that a module-level orientation is at most one short paragraph. The `present-tense-prose` invariant puts change-relative narration in commit messages and issue history. Planned, deferred and excluded scope is work-tracking content.

Existing sources drift from this contract. Comment lines make up 17–45% of each crate's Rust lines; hundreds of comment lines carry narration or scope markers (non-goals, out of scope, deferred to, phase or wave designators, task and story references, legacy and migration language), and hundreds more embed tracker short IDs as provenance.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-21: Every Rust file under `crates/` (sources, tests, benches, examples and build scripts) meets the root `AGENTS.md` comment rule: no comment restates the adjacent code, and each module-level doc is at most one short orientation paragraph plus the contract statements its public API needs.
- [hard] REQ-22: No comment or Rustdoc narrates history or process: commit, task, story, phase, wave or session designators, old/new contrasts, legacy or migration language, and design-history provenance are absent.
- [hard] REQ-23: No comment or Rustdoc states planned, deferred, excluded or out-of-scope work. Where such a statement described a current limitation, the limitation is restated in the present tense (for example as a panic or supported-domain condition), and the planned work exists as a tracked issue.
- [hard] REQ-24: A case-insensitive grep of `crates/` comment lines for the pattern below returns only lines listed, each with a one-line justification, in the story's linked completion record.

  ```text
  non-goal|out of scope|not in scope|future work|deferred to|follow-on|phase [a-e]\b|wave [a-z0-9]|(task|issue|story) `?[0-9a-f]{8}|previously|no longer|legacy|migrat
  ```

- [hard] REQ-25: Public API Rustdoc still states purpose, panics, safety conditions and non-obvious complexity; Rustdoc builds without new warnings and the Rust CI gate passes.
- [hard] REQ-26: The change contains only comment, Rustdoc and whitespace edits, verified by an ignore-whitespace diff review of every hunk.
- [hard] REQ-27: The linked completion record reports each crate's comment-line share before and after the sweep, and lists every tracked issue created or matched under REQ-23.
- [hard] REQ-28: Every Rust file under `dev/tools/` meets REQ-21, REQ-22 and REQ-23 through comment, Rustdoc and whitespace edits only.

## Notes

Generated data tables (for example LDPC parity-check constants) keep their provenance headers. Comments that cite an external standard, paper or committed receipt are evidence pointers and remain, in shortened form. Criterion IDs begin at REQ-21 and stay stable.



## Decisions

- DEC-01: The owner decided on 2026-10-04 that a behavior-preserving hunk which `rustfmt` or `clippy` forces after a comment deletion (array layout, a trailing comma, dropped braces, a collapsed nested `if`) is inside the sweep and consistent with REQ-26, provided the unit's commit body names the hunk. The owner also approved one string-literal edit in `crates/gf2-kernels-hip/build.rs`, recorded as DEC-01 on issue 93aed46a.
title: Workspace source-comment tersification sweep
